title: Benchmark harness: continuous-batching and queueing under mixed workloads
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Objective: build a reproducible load-testing and benchmarking harness to quantify how continuous batching and request queueing interact under mixed customer-like workloads, and to create automatic regression detection for tokens/sec and p95 latency. This ticket covers spec, harness implementation, baseline runs, dashboarding, and CI gating for regressions.

Why: we currently lack systematic experiments that vary batch-window heuristics, per-model inflight limits, and mixed-length traffic mixes to show where batching improves tokens/sec but increases p95 for tail-sensitive applications. Without this we risk tuning defaults that reduce latency for interactive flows or increase cost unpredictably under real traffic mixes.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness (containerized) that can replay configurable mixed workloads: short-chat, long-complete, and embedding bursts
Metrics exported to Prometheus format and collected in existing metrics pipeline (or test-specific pushgateway)
Baseline nightly job that runs 3x and stores summary artifacts in s3://redwood-benchmarks/ENG-4372/<date>/
Dashboards showing tokens/sec, requests/sec, p95/p99 latency, batch size distribution, queue depth over time for each run
Automatic regression detector: flags runs where tokens/sec drops >10% vs 30-day median or p95 increases >15% and opens a templated ENG ticket
Runbook and README with instructions to reproduce locally and on CI
implementation_notes: Harness architecture: a loadgen service (Go) + scenario driver (YAML) + result aggregator. Use gRPC/HTTP to call the Redwood API endpoint under test; support both hosted and dedicated endpoints behind a switch.

Workload mix definitions: 60% short-chat (32-128 tokens), 30% long-complete (1024-4096 tokens), 10% embedding/bulk calls (embedding size 1536). Support configurable seed distribution for prompt tokens and response lengths.

Continuous batching knobs to vary: batching window (ms), max_batch_tokens, max_batch_requests, per-device inflight limit. The harness sweeps these parameters across a grid and records metrics per-config.
Queueing model: measure queue_length_gauge and request_age_histogram; optionally inject artificial CPU/GPU contention to observe backpressure behaviors.
Cache priming: tests must include a warmup phase that primes KV cache for conversational flows. Warmup duration default 300s, configurable.
Measuring tokens/sec: use metric inference.tokens_processed_total and compute slope over steady-state window (exclude warmup and cooldown). Report median and 95% CI across repeats.
Latency p95: compute from histogram metric inference.latency_seconds_bucket. For HTTP flows include end-to-end client-observed latency and server-side scheduling latency if available.
Regression detection: baseline computed as 30-day rolling median per-config. Regression rules configurable in YAML. On trigger, attach run artifacts and flamegraph snapshots to generated ticket.

Instrumentation: expose these metric names: inference.tokens_processed_total, inference.requests_total, inference.latency_p95_seconds, batching.batch_size_histogram, batching.batch_wait_ms_summary, queue.length_gauge, scheduler.inflight_requests_gauge.
Storage: test artifacts and raw traces uploaded to s3 path. Summary JSON saved and uploaded to metrics bucket and indexed in internal bench DB for historical query.
Security: run non-production tokens and point to a dedicated test model/service. security_review_required: false for harness infra, but require gating for any runs targeting production endpoints.
test_plan: Step 1: Implement loadgen + scenario driver and containerize. Provide example scenarios in /scenarios/mixed-default.yaml.
Step 2: Add Prometheus exporter to aggregator and validate metric names locally with a mini-cluster (1 GPU serving node).
Step 3: Define grid for batching window [0, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 ms], max_batch_tokens [512, 1024, 2048], inflight_limits [8, 16, 32]. Run single sweep with short run length (600s).
Step 4: Select top 6 interesting configs from sweep and run 3x each for 1800s to collect steady-state results. Upload artifacts and create baseline entries.
Step 5: Integrate regression detector to compare nightly run results with 30-day baseline, set up alerting to #eng-perf and create an automated ticket template for regressions.
Step 6: Validate with an internal canary using real production traces (anonymized) if opt-in from privacy/infra teams. Document results and recommended default heuristics.
Step 7: Publish dashboard and runbook; schedule recurring job in CI (nightly) and add as optional pre-merge check for runtime changes.
metrics_collected: batch_size distribution and mean batch wait time
queue length over time and request age distribution
GPU utilization and memory footprint (from exporter)
KV cache hit ratio for conversational flows
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Raman: Created ticket; initial spec drafted and reviewed with performance team. Decided to prioritize mixed workloads (short/long/embeddings) to reflect customer traces.

2026-03-11 Diego Marquez: Completed initial loadgen prototype (Go). Using async HTTP + token accounting. Pushed branch bench-harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/tree/ENG-4372-proto

2026-03-12 Priya Desai (review): Feedback: add end-to-end and server-side latency separation, and include GPU util metrics. Also suggested including an experiment to vary KV cache TTL to measure cache impact on batch hit rates.

2026-03-13 Diego Marquez: Ran first sweep on a 1-GPU test cluster. Observations: aggressive batching window (50ms) increases tokens/sec by ~27% for long-complete heavy mixes but p95 for short-chat increased by ~42ms. Uploaded preliminary results to s3.

2026-03-14 Aisha Raman: Decided acceptance thresholds for regression detector. Created template for automated ticket generation. Next: scale sweep to 4-GPU cluster and run 3x per-config for robust baselines. Assigned infra request to provision a 4-GPU ephemeral cluster (INFRA-98).
